sections.h2: Which Mount Vernon offices handle a Rockcastle County tax account?
sections.html:
The work is divided among three counters near the courthouse. The Property Valuation Administration values parcels and answers at (606) 256-4194, using P.O. Box 977, Mt. Vernon, KY 40456 as its mailing address. The sheriff bills and collects from 205 E. Main St., Box 2, at (606) 256-2032. The County Clerk, at (606) 256-2831 and Box 6 in that building, receives any bill that goes delinquent.

No one of the three sets a rate. The Rockcastle County Fiscal Court helps, meeting monthly on the second Tuesday at 1:00 p.m. inside the courthouse, and a resident who wishes to speak asks for a slot a day in advance. School and special districts choose their own levies, and the sheriff bills the total.

The county says every official record of its government is kept by the County Clerk, so a deed or lien search begins there. The Fiscal Court also runs an occupational tax office at (606) 256-8374 for employers, and the county health department, the dog warden and the solid waste office keep their own numbers for matters that sometimes come up when a house changes hands, such as trash service and animal control.

sections.h2: Which dates matter on a Rockcastle County tax bill?
sections.html:
KRS 134.015 makes December 31 the due date and names the sheriff as the collector. Barring a delayed mailing that shifts the calendar, the stages run in this order:

  • Through November 1: the whole bill paid at once is cut by 2 percent.
  • Early November through year end: only the printed figure is owed.
  • Throughout January: 5 percent is added.
  • From February: 10 percent is added, plus a sheriff's fee that Department of Revenue examples include.
  • Close of April 15: the sheriff stops collecting and passes the leftovers to the clerk, with a lien attached.

The shifted calendar gives a month for the discount, a month at face value and a month at 5 percent. The bill itself shows which one applies. Values are fixed as of January 1, so a late winter closing normally leaves the prior year's bill under the seller's name. Get the exact payoff from the sheriff before closing day.

sections.h2: What might a Rockcastle County home cost to carry?
sections.html:
Kentucky trimmed its 2025 real estate rate to 10.6 cents for every hundred dollars of assessment. Census QuickFacts puts a typical Rockcastle County house at $123,600, so the state's cut of that is about $131.02. School, county and district rates sit above it, and only the sheriff's bill for a given address shows the sum.

Older and disabled owners receive a deduction that shrinks the base. Take $49,100 away and $74,500 remains, which lowers the state cut to about $78.97. On a house this size the deduction removes a big share of the value, so a qualifying owner gains by filing at the PVA early.

A sale changes the picture. The bill follows whoever held the parcel when the year began, so the contract should assign the year in writing, and any open balance belongs at the closing table.

sections.h2: What steps does a Rockcastle County appeal follow?
sections.html:
Start at the PVA office, because no appeal can be filed until you have met with staff there. Staff must walk you through the law, the procedure and how your number was derived, and a written record captures your claim and the outcome.

  • Watch for the published inspection notice. The roll opens on May's first Monday and can be viewed for thirteen days.
  • Meet staff in that window, or sooner if an assessment notice has already arrived.
  • File the appeal with the clerk the next workday after viewing ends.
  • Attend the local board hearing, which convenes about a month after viewing.

The board weighs only evidence shown with both sides present. Insurance papers, construction costs, listings and property descriptions qualify as proof, and a case without them fails. If the board sets a number above yours after bills are out, a supplemental bill arrives.

sections.h2: Which Rockcastle County owners get a tax break?
sections.html:
Homeowners from age 65, along with owners whose total disability is recognized by a federal or retirement program, can take the homestead deduction on their residence. The figure is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. File with the PVA, along with a license, passport or similar proof of age.

An age claim stays in force while the first applicant keeps living there. Most disability claims must be refiled each year, but veterans with service-connected disability and people permanently disabled under Social Security or the state retirement system are excused. A couple counts as one claimant, and a purchaser files separately because the break travels with the person.

Churches, schools, charities and governments may be exempt altogether under sections 170 and 171 of the Kentucky Constitution, after an application to the PVA.

sections.h2: What do unpaid Rockcastle County taxes turn into?
sections.html:
Delinquency starts as April 15 ends. The sheriff forwards the list to the County Clerk, each bill turns into a certificate of delinquency, and the lien in KRS 134.420 survives eleven years, through any resale of the house.

Each month adds 1 percent, and commissions for the clerk and the county attorney follow. In the state's sample, a $1,000 bill grows to $1,254.00 on transfer and $1,611.30 once the attorney's first letter has gone out. The statute puts the sale between three and four and a half months after transfer, with a 30-day letter before it, a second letter if needed and newspaper advertising of at least 30 days.

Whoever buys a certificate can add costs. Paying the sheriff before the April deadline keeps the figure small.

sections.h2: How do Rockcastle County's housing figures look?
sections.html:
Rockcastle County was founded in 1810 and named for the Rockcastle River, whose own name comes from its rock cliffs. The seat, Mount Vernon, was founded in 1789 and is the largest city, and Brodhead and Livingston are the other towns. The county spans about 317 square miles of land, partly in the Daniel Boone National Forest, and sits inside the Richmond-Berea micropolitan area. Garrard, Madison, Lincoln, Jackson, Pulaski and Laurel counties are its neighbors.

The 2020 census counted 7,321 housing units, with 10.6 percent of them vacant, and 74.8 percent of occupied units were lived in by their owners. A renter vacancy rate of 6.3 percent was reported. Every resident counted as rural that year, and the middle age was 44.1. Workers commute 26.4 minutes on average, and 80 percent of households have a broadband plan. A house with pending repairs or an outstanding lien can be sold for cash as it stands, with the lien paid at closing.

faqs.q: Where do I send a Rockcastle County tax payment?
faqs.a: To the sheriff's office at 205 E. Main St., Box 2, Mount Vernon, (606) 256-2032. The PVA at (606) 256-4194 only assesses and does not collect.

faqs.q: How much does early payment save in Rockcastle County?
faqs.a: Two percent of the bill when all of it arrives by November 1 on the regular schedule. Afterward only the printed amount is owed until year end, and penalties begin in January.

faqs.q: What is the older owner deduction in Rockcastle County?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, deducted from the assessed value. Owners at 65 or beyond, or with a total disability, apply through the PVA.

faqs.q: When can I speak to the Rockcastle County Fiscal Court?
faqs.a: At its monthly meeting on the second Tuesday, 1:00 p.m., in the courthouse. Give 24 hours of notice to be placed on the agenda.

faqs.q: What if my Rockcastle County bill remains unpaid after April 15?
faqs.a: The County Clerk receives it as a certificate of delinquency with a lien. Interest starts at 1 percent a month, and the clerk and attorney commissions are added.
